interventions.name: Rooftop rainwater harvesting for use
interventions.summary: Collect roof runoff through gutters and a first-flush diverter into a tank for later use.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
Some places require harvesting on new buildings.
maintenance: Clean gutters, filter and first-flush diverter before and during the rainy season.
Keep the tank covered and clean it periodically.
interventions.construction: Gutters, downpipes, a filter and a tank; no excavation unless the tank is underground.
interventions.benefit_note: Water is available only after rain falls once the system is built; supply in dry months depends on tank size.

effect_inputs.label: Share of roof rainfall that reaches the tank and is used
effect_inputs.note: Losses from first flush, spills and overflow when the tank is full.

effect_inputs.label: Rainfall in a typical year (millimetres)
effect_inputs.note: Used only when no rainfall source covers a full year here.

cautions: Harvested water used for drinking needs treatment and testing.

wider_effects.mechanism: Less roof runoff reaches drains: this can ease local flooding, and can also reduce water reaching streams or recharge downstream.
wider_effects.matters_when: Many roofs in the catchment harvest, or downstream users rely on that runoff.

reviews.reason: Before harvested water is used for drinking or cooking.
If the tank sits on a roof or is built underground.

interventions.name: Rooftop runoff recharge pit
interventions.summary: Route filtered roof runoff into a pit or trench so it soaks into the ground.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
maintenance: Clean the filter media and remove silt after heavy rain.
interventions.construction: Excavate a pit or trench, fill with filter media, connect downpipes.
interventions.benefit_note: Any groundwater response builds up over one or more wet seasons and is not guaranteed locally.
cautions: Only roof water: keep away from sewage, septic tanks and polluted runoff.
Recharge can carry contaminants into groundwater without filtering.

wider_effects.mechanism: Water soaking into the ground may add to groundwater that others also draw on.
wider_effects.matters_when: The ground lets water through and the aquifer below is used by others.

wider_effects.mechanism: Runoff that is not clean can carry contaminants into groundwater that others may drink.
wider_effects.matters_when: The runoff picks up pollution, or wells nearby draw from shallow groundwater.

reviews.reason: Check the soil takes water and the water table is deep enough.
Check the runoff is clean enough to put into the ground.

interventions.name: Recharge well or shaft
interventions.summary: A deeper shaft that lets filtered runoff reach permeable layers.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
Deep shafts often need approval from the local water or groundwater authority.
maintenance: Desilt the shaft and renew the filter periodically.
interventions.construction: Drill or dig a lined shaft with a silt trap and filter.
interventions.benefit_note: Depends on soil and aquifer conditions that need a local survey.
cautions: Needs a site survey of soil, aquifer and nearby pollution sources.

wider_effects.mechanism: Water soaking into the ground may add to groundwater that others also draw on.
wider_effects.matters_when: The ground lets water through and the aquifer below is used by others.

wider_effects.mechanism: Runoff that is not clean can carry contaminants into groundwater that others may drink.
wider_effects.matters_when: The runoff picks up pollution, or wells nearby draw from shallow groundwater.

reviews.reason: A shaft reaches deeper layers directly; the aquifer and nearby wells need a survey.
Water entering a shaft bypasses soil filtering.
Drilling or digging and lining a shaft.

interventions.name: Leak detection and repair
interventions.summary: Find and fix leaks in pipes, tanks, valves and fittings.
permissions: Work on public mains is for the utility; private pipes are the owner's.
maintenance: Repeat checks periodically; leaks recur as pipes age.
interventions.construction: A survey, then repairs; buried pipes may need digging.
interventions.benefit_note: Savings start once repairs are done; their size depends on how much is leaking, which needs measuring.

effect_inputs.label: Share of piped supply lost to leaks
effect_inputs.note: From a water audit or meter comparison.

effect_inputs.label: Share of those losses the repairs stop

cautions: Without metering the leak volume, savings cannot be estimated.

wider_effects.mechanism: Water no longer lost to leaks can stay in the network for others.
wider_effects.matters_when: The leaks are on pipes shared with others.

wider_effects.mechanism: Leaking pipes can feed shallow groundwater; stopping them may lower it slightly where they did.
wider_effects.matters_when: Shallow wells nearby depend on water from leaking pipes.

interventions.name: Greywater reuse
interventions.summary: Treat water from basins, showers and laundry for non-drinking uses such as toilet flushing or gardens.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
Reuse rules and treatment standards vary by place.
maintenance: Regular cleaning of filters and treatment units.
interventions.construction: Separate drain and supply pipes, a treatment unit and a tank.
interventions.benefit_note: Savings start once the system runs.

effect_inputs.label: Share of remaining water use that treated greywater can replace
effect_inputs.note: Typically flushing and garden use only.

cautions: Poor treatment is a health risk.

wider_effects.mechanism: Less wastewater returns to drains or sewers, which can change the flow others downstream receive.
wider_effects.matters_when: Downstream users or treatment works rely on that flow.

reviews.reason: The treatment must meet the local reuse standard for its use.

interventions.name: Water-efficient fixtures
interventions.summary: Low-flow taps and showers, dual-flush toilets and similar fittings.
interventions.benefit_note: Savings start once fittings are replaced; their size depends on current use.

effect_inputs.label: Share of water use the fixtures save
effect_inputs.note: Depends on which fixtures are replaced and how they are used.

wider_effects.mechanism: Drawing less from a shared supply can leave more water or pressure for others on the same network.
wider_effects.matters_when: The site is on a supply network that others also depend on.

interventions.name: Metering and demand awareness
interventions.summary: Meter use and share it so households can see and reduce consumption.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
Meters on utility connections are the utility's.
maintenance: Read and maintain meters; keep sharing results.
interventions.construction: Install meters and set up reading and feedback.
interventions.benefit_note: Any saving depends on how people respond and is not assumed.

effect_inputs.label: Share of water use saved by metering and feedback
effect_inputs.note: Savings can fade without continued feedback.

wider_effects.mechanism: Drawing less from a shared supply can leave more water or pressure for others on the same network.
wider_effects.matters_when: The site is on a supply network that others also depend on.

interventions.name: Additional storage
interventions.summary: More tank capacity to bridge gaps between supply days.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
Rooftop tanks may need a structural check.
interventions.construction: Install a tank and connect it.
interventions.benefit_note: Storage shifts when water is available; it adds no water.

wider_effects.mechanism: Filling large tanks while supply runs can lower pressure for others on the same network.
wider_effects.matters_when: Supply is intermittent and shared, and many tanks fill at once.

reviews.reason: If the tank sits on a roof or raised stand.

interventions.name: Stormwater detention and permeable surfaces
interventions.summary: Slow and hold storm runoff with permeable paving, swales or detention areas.
permissions: Check local building, water and planning rules before work starts.
Changes to drains or public land need the local authority.
maintenance: Clear silt and litter; keep surfaces permeable.
interventions.benefit_note: Effect appears in storms after construction; its size needs local drainage data.

wider_effects.mechanism: Holding storm runoff can reduce flooding downstream, and it also delays or reduces water reaching downstream channels.
wider_effects.matters_when: Downstream areas flood, or rely on storm flows.

wider_effects.mechanism: Street and yard runoff soaking in can carry oil, metals and other pollutants into groundwater.
wider_effects.matters_when: The runoff comes from roads or polluted surfaces, or wells draw from shallow groundwater nearby.

reviews.reason: Where runoff is meant to soak in near wells.
